newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran's Tabriz petrochemical plant running - paper.
newsitem.headline: Iran's Tabriz petrochemical plant running - paper.

text.p: Iran's new petrochemical plant near the northwestern city of Tabriz has started operation, a newspaper said on Thursday.
The daily Resalat quoted Abbas Sedqi, the manager of the complex, as saying the first phase of the plant had started production at an annual capacity of 405,000 tonnes of petrochemical byproducts.
The output would include 136,000 tonnes of ethylene, 56,000 tonnes of propylene, 100,000 tonnes of polyethylene and 55,000 tonnes of benzene and a variety of aromatics, Sedqi said.
The second phase of the project, with an annual capacity of 95,000 tonnes, would come onstream in the new Iranian year which starts on March 21, he added.
Sedqi said hard currency shortages and non-payment of sums by "foreign firms" were among reasons for a delay in the plant's completion, the newspaper reported. He did not elaborate.
Iran is the Middle East's second largest petrochemical producer after Saudi Arabia and aims to triple its annual output to 30 million tonnes in 25 years.

Under Iran's current five-year plan (1995-2000) the National Petrochemical Company (NPC) is to increase capacity to 15 million tonnes from the present 10 million tonnes with the construction of five new petrochemical plants.

The Tabriz plant has cost $1.106 billion in hard cash plus 2,100 billion rials ($1.2 billion) to build and would save Iran $1 million in hard currency spending on petrochemical imports, officials have said.
($1=1,750 rials at the rate used for state budget accounts)
